Kazi Mosharraf Hossain ----- Petitioner
vs

full_judgment:
Md Imman Ali J : This Rule Nisi was issued upon an application filed under Article 102(2)- (a)(ii) of the Constitution, calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the continuation of the proceedings of Special Case No. 6 of 2008 under section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 arising out of Metropolitan Durniti Daman Bishesh Tribunal Case No. 6 of 2003 corresponding to Mohammadpur Police Station Case No. 60 dated 26-7-2000 lodged under section. 5(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act 1957 now pending in the Court of Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. The facts of the case relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that the petitioner, who was the President of the Collective Bargaining Agent (CBA) of DESA, was implicated in Mohammadpur Police Station Case No. 60 dated 26-7-2000 under section 5(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1957 (AC Act 1957). After the due investigation police submitted final report No. 131 dated 20-5-2003 under section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, but the same was not accepted by the Tribunal and cognizance was taken by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1 on 9-7-2003 of an offence under section 5(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1957 (sic). Clearly the name of the relevant law has been wrongly quoted and should read "Anti-Corruption Act, 1957." The petitioner then moved the matter before the High Court Division in an application under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10897 of 2003. The Rule in that case was discharged on 22-8-2005 and the matter was then taken before the Appellate Division and it is still pending there. While the matter was pending before the High Court Division the further proceedings of the trial were stayed. However, when no further impediment was present for proceeding with the trial, on 16-9-2007 a prayer was made on behalf of the prosecution for further investigation. Thereafter, on 12-2-2008 a supplementary charge sheet was filed and accepted by the Court on 18-2-2008 and cognizance was taken of an offence under section 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (ACC Act, 2004). Charge was framed against the accused by the Divisional Special Judge on 28-8-2008 for an offence under the said section. Thereafter, PW 1 was examined on 9-9-2008 and on 14-10-2008 the petitioner moved the High Court Division challenging the further proceedings of the case. 

 3. Mr Md Ruhul Quddus, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, points out that on 11-2-2008 one Md Habibur Rahman, the Commissioner (Investigation) of the Anti-Corruption Commission, respondent No. 3, under Memo No. যাচাই/২৭-৯৯(টাঃফোঃ-২/২০০৬ dated 11-2-2008 issued a purported sanction for submitting the investigation report i.e. the supplementary charge sheet, against the petitioner. He submits that the said sanction is not a sanction as required by section 32 read with section 17(nya) of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007, (ACC Rules, 2007) and, as such, the further proceeding of the case is without lawful authority. He points out that the requirement of law is that it must be the Commission, meaning all 3 (three) members of the Anti-Corruption Commission, who grant sanction for the proceeding and the sanction accorded by only one member is no sanction in the eye of law. 

 4. The learned Advocate then refers us to section 38(4) of the ACC Act, 2004, which relates to the repeal of the Anti-Corruption (Tribunal) Ordinance, 1960 and submits that on the repeal of the previous law and coming into force of the present law, the case was liable to he transferred immediately to the Court of the Special Judge in the relevant area. He points out that from the order sheets of the Tribunal it appears that instead of transferring the case to the Court of Special Judge, the Tribunal continued to deal with the case and passed orders which are all without jurisdiction. He submits that the failure of the Court having seisin of the case to transfer the same to the appropriate Special Judge's Court, any further proceeding of the case was without jurisdiction and unlawful. He submits that, therefore, the further proceeding of the case is illegal and without lawful authority. 

 6. On the first issue raised by the petitioner with regard to the sanction, the learned Advocate for the Anti-Corruption Commission refers us to section 15 of the ACC Act, 2004 and submits that it is the Commission who will take all decisions in its meetings. Then he refers to section 1741 and submits that the Commission will decide how the corruption will be investigated and the case lodged and also as to fixing the mode of approval. He then refers to Rule 15(1) of the ACC Rules, 2007 and submits that the power of granting approval or sanction shall be exercised by the Commission or by someone empowered by the Commission in that behalf. He also refers to Rule 15(7) and submits that the authorised person will accord his approval in Form 3. The learned Advocate points out that Form 3 contemplates the signature of only one Commissioner. The learned Advocate submits that, therefore, the accordance of sanction by only one Commissioner is very much in accordance with the law and the Rules. 

 7. With regard to the transfer of the case under section 38(4), Mr Aziz Khan submits that the Sessions Judge is an ex-officio Special Judge and, therefore, there is no necessity to transfer the case, since he is himself Special Judge, and this, he submits, is apparent from the order dated 13-2-2008, where Md Azizul Huq, the pre-siding Judge, is described as the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka and in the following order dated 18-2-2008 the selfsame Judge is described as the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka. The learned Advocate further points out that although the ACC Act, 2004 came into force on 9-5-2004, no special Judges were designated as such until the notification dated 25-4-2007 and, therefore, there was no possibility for the Sessions Judge in seisin of the case to transfer the case to the Court of Special Judge. However, he candidly admits that the orders subsequent to 25-4-2007, i.e. orders dated 16-9-2007, 29-10-2007, 22-11-2007, 3-1-2008 and 13-2-2008, were signed by Md Azizul Huq as a Tribunal Judge and as a Metropolitan Sessions Judge, and this was done possibly in error. But he submits that the fact remains that Md Azizul Huq, who was the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, was also the Ex-officio Metropolitan Senior Special Judge. Furthermore, he submits, no prejudice was done to the accused petitioner by the order passed by Md Azizul Huq on those dates mentioned.
